title: The strategic role of operations
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:32Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: No point in the bank covers how operations give a competitive edge through cost leadership or differentiation; the closest, on customers, suppliers and competitors, is a broader Year 11 idea about market forces.

draft.title: The strategic role of operations
card: A business has a strategic role for operations when it uses the way it makes its goods or services to beat its competitors. Operations can create this edge in two main ways.
the business aims to have the lowest costs in its market, so it can charge the lowest prices. It does this with bulk buying, efficient processes and little waste.
the business aims to be different or better than its competitors, in quality, design, features or service. Customers may then choose it for those reasons, not for price alone.
A business can choose one approach as its main focus. The choice shapes how it designs its processes, buys inputs and sets quality standards.
draft.remember: Operations can win an edge by being the cheapest or by being different or better.

a.q: Which operations decision is an example of cost leadership?
opts: Buying inputs in bulk to cut the cost of each unit
Hand finishing each product to a higher standard
Adding a unique feature that rivals do not offer
Offering personal service to each customer
a.why: Bulk buying lowers the cost of each unit, which lets the business charge the lowest prices. The other options aim to make the business different or better, which is differentiation. Hand finishing is tempting, but it adds cost and is not a way to be cheapest.
a.clue: Which choice helps the business become the cheapest in its market?

b.q: Priya runs a bakery in Orange. Her ovens bake sourdough from locally milled organic flour, and she charges more than the nearby supermarket. How does her operations approach give her an edge?
opts: Differentiation, because the product is better or different
Cost leadership, because her inputs are local
Cost leadership, because she sells fewer loaves
Differentiation, because her prices are higher
b.why: Priya's organic, locally milled flour makes her bread different from the supermarket's, so she competes on differentiation. The higher price is a result of this choice and is not what makes it differentiation. Local inputs do not make her the cheapest, so cost leadership is wrong.
b.clue: Ask whether she is competing by being cheapest or by being different.

a.best: Buying inputs in bulk to cut the cost of each unit

b.best: Differentiation, because the product is better or different
